data.title: Ward 18 2021 Flood — Full Incident Retrospective
data.outcomeSummary: Overall response reduced projected risk by roughly 40%, but the single highest-cost failure was the pump/outfall mismatch (see HIST-2021-11-W18) — the traffic and emergency response components performed well in isolation.
data.lessonLearned: A coordinated response can still underperform if even one department's action targets the wrong constraint — partial success on 3 of 4 fronts is not the same as success.

data.title: Ward 18 Flash Flood & Hospital Road Paralysis
data.outcomeSummary: Mobile pumps deployed to Ward 18 in 2021, but risk was reduced only 8% because the storm drain outfall was already submerged by canal backflow — the pumps had nowhere to discharge to.
data.lessonLearned: Pump deployment is ineffective once the outfall is submerged — check outfall status before committing pump units, not just drain saturation.

data.title: Cyclone Michaung — Coastal Ward Storm Surge + Rainfall
data.outcomeSummary: Airport and multiple hospital access roads flooded; power outages disabled traffic signals city-wide for 14+ hours, compounding gridlock during evacuation.
data.lessonLearned: Power infrastructure stress must trigger traffic-signal contingency planning before outage occurs, not after — signal failure during evacuation is a compounding, not independent, risk.
